articles.title: Design for Understandability
articles.summary: Design for Understandability is a talk given by a speaker at Google's internal Code Health Summit, where the speaker emphasizes the importance of understanding code in a world where Large Language Models (LLMs) generate much of it. The speaker argues that without understanding, LLMs are little more than complexity-generating machines, and that human Software Engineers (SWEs) must take on the responsibility of judgment to ensure code is maintainable and healthy. By using design principles such as design by contract, class invariants, and modularity, SWEs can create systems that are easier to understand and maintain.

articles.title: Mutex poisoning is not for everyone
articles.summary: Mutex poisoning is a technique used to handle a specific type of error that can occur when a mutex is released abnormally, but it can also lead to unexpected behavior and poor code readability. This technique is often used in low-level programming to handle rare and unusual errors, but it can also be misused to introduce unnecessary complexity and bad code patterns. In general, mutex poisoning is not a recommended approach for most applications, as it can significantly pessimize code performance and make code harder to understand.
